c055.back: Only explicitly defined NOT NULL. No PK, UNIQUE, FK, CHECK, indexes or DEFAULT values.
c055.try_sql:
-- Copy employees with CTAS and compare the constraints of both tables
CREATE TABLE lab_c055_emp AS SELECT * FROM employees;
SELECT table_name, constraint_type, COUNT(*) AS ile
FROM   user_constraints
WHERE  table_name IN ('EMPLOYEES', 'LAB_C055_EMP')
GROUP  BY table_name, constraint_type
ORDER  BY table_name, constraint_type;

c056.front: Where can NOT NULL be defined?
c056.back: Only at column level (inline). The other constraints can be at column or table level. A multi-column key must be at table level.

c057.front: ON DELETE CASCADE or SET NULL?
c057.back: CASCADE deletes the children along with the parent. SET NULL writes NULL into the FK column of the children. By default, deleting a parent that has children is rejected (ORA-02292).

c058.back: From -999.99 to 999.99. Extra digits after the decimal point are rounded, for example 12.345 → 12.35. Too many digits before the decimal point → ORA-01438.

c059.back: VARCHAR2: variable length, max 4000 bytes (standard). CHAR: fixed length, padded with spaces, max 2000 bytes.
c059.try_sql:
-- CHAR(5) pads with spaces to 5 characters, VARCHAR2(5) keeps only 2
SELECT LENGTH(CAST('ab' AS CHAR(5)))     AS dlugosc_char,
       LENGTH(CAST('ab' AS VARCHAR2(5))) AS dlugosc_varchar2
FROM   dual;

c060.front: DROP TABLE and the recycle bin?
c060.back: DROP moves the table to the recycle bin. FLASHBACK TABLE t TO BEFORE DROP restores it. DROP ... PURGE skips the bin: the table can no longer be recovered.

c061.back: It drops a column logically: fast and forever (it cannot be undone). Later ALTER TABLE ... DROP UNUSED COLUMNS removes it physically.

c062.back: ALTER TABLE t READ ONLY blocks DML. DROP TABLE still works. ALTER TABLE t READ WRITE allows writing again.

c510.front: ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY a column: what is allowed when there is data?
c510.back: Widening: always. Narrowing: only when every value fits (otherwise ORA-01441). Changing the data type: only when the column is empty (otherwise ORA-01439).

c511.back: DEFAULT works only when you leave the column out (or write DEFAULT). An explicit NULL stays NULL. DEFAULT ON NULL (12c+) also replaces an explicit NULL with the default value.

c512.front: What restrictions does DROP COLUMN have?
c512.back: You cannot drop the last column (ORA-12983). A column of a key that an FK points to needs CASCADE CONSTRAINTS. Several columns at once: DROP (a, b). It is DDL, so no ROLLBACK.

c513.back: CREATE PRIVATE TEMPORARY TABLE ora$ptt_name ...: the definition and data exist only for your session, in memory. The default is ON COMMIT DROP DEFINITION (it disappears after the transaction). PRESERVE DEFINITION keeps it until the end of the session.

c514.front: What can you not do with an external table?
c514.back: No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, no indexes and no enforced keys. The data stays in a file on the system and is read at every query. You load it with CTAS or INSERT ... SELECT.

c515.back: NOVALIDATE: checks only future DML, old rows may break the rule. VALIDATE (the default with ENABLE): checks all rows. DISABLE ... CASCADE also disables the dependent foreign keys.
c515.try_sql:
-- Without extra options, constraints are ENABLED and VALIDATED (all rows checked)
SELECT constraint_name, constraint_type, status, validated
FROM   user_constraints
WHERE  table_name = 'EMPLOYEES'
ORDER  BY constraint_name;

c1550.front: What can a private temporary table not have?
c1550.back: Constraints (not even NOT NULL), DEFAULT values and indexes: ORA-14451. CTAS works. The name must start with ORA$PTT_. Creating one does not commit.

c1551.front: Where in the data dictionary do you find private temporary tables?
c1551.back: In USER_PRIVATE_TEMP_TABLES (DURATION TRANSACTION or SESSION). They are not in USER_TABLES. Global temporary tables are in USER_TABLES with TEMPORARY = 'Y'.

c1552.front: ALTER or DROP a global temporary table while sessions have rows in it?
c1552.back: It fails: ORA-14450 (ALTER) / ORA-14452 (DROP). Each session must first COMMIT (DELETE ROWS), or end / TRUNCATE (PRESERVE ROWS). TRUNCATE clears only your rows.

c1553.front: Global temporary tables and foreign keys?
c1553.back: Not allowed: ORA-14455. PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK and NOT NULL are allowed on a GTT.

c1554.front: External table: what is checked at CREATE, and what at query time?
c1554.back: CREATE checks the syntax and the DIRECTORY object (missing: ORA-06564). The file itself is opened only when you query the table.
c1554.try_sql:
-- CREATE checks the DIRECTORY object: it is missing here, so ORA-06564 (nobody looks for the file yet)
CREATE TABLE lab_c1554_ext (id NUMBER, name VARCHAR2(30))
ORGANIZATION EXTERNAL (
  TYPE ORACLE_LOADER
  DEFAULT DIRECTORY lab_c1554_dir
  LOCATION ('dane.csv')
);

c1555.back: ORACLE_LOADER: reads text files, read-only. ORACLE_DATAPUMP: reads and writes binary dump files, so CREATE TABLE ... ORGANIZATION EXTERNAL ... AS SELECT can unload data to a file.

c1556.front: REJECT LIMIT in an external table?
c1556.back: How many bad records a query can survive. The default is 0: the first rejected record ends the query with an error. UNLIMITED: bad records are skipped (they land in the bad file).

c1557.front: Drop a column that is part of a multi-column constraint?
c1557.back: ORA-12991 (the same for SET UNUSED). Add CASCADE CONSTRAINTS: the whole constraint is dropped, not reduced to the remaining columns.

c1558.front: After SET UNUSED (note): can you add a new column note? Can you DROP COLUMN note?
c1558.back: Add: yes, the name is free at once (the old column gets a hidden name SYS_C...$). DROP COLUMN note: ORA-00904; use DROP UNUSED COLUMNS.

c1559.front: DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED: when is the constraint checked?
c1559.back: At COMMIT (or at SET CONSTRAINT ... IMMEDIATE). Breaking the rule at COMMIT raises ORA-02091 and rolls back the whole transaction. Deferrability cannot be added later.

c1560.back: GENERATED ALWAYS: you cannot supply your own value (ORA-32795 on INSERT, ORA-32796 on UPDATE). BY DEFAULT: your own value is OK, an explicit NULL is not. BY DEFAULT ON NULL: NULL gets the next value. One identity column per table.

c1561.front: CTAS with a column list: what can be in that list?
c1561.back: New column names and constraints (for example id PRIMARY KEY), one name for each selected column (otherwise ORA-01730). No data types (ORA-01773). DEFAULT and identity are never copied.
